messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT detected: continuous batching latency cliff in west-2 (p95 > 2s) :warning:
oncall-bot: Affected service: inference-runtime, route: /v1/generate, tag: prod-dedicated-1
oncall-bot: auto-page -> eng-oncall, paging policy: high-latency

sarah (oncall): seeing it on our dashboards too, p50 ~600ms now but p95 jumping to 2.3s
Aj: noticing queue depth spike on host pool 42-45, microbatch sizes collapse then spike 
Leo: KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 47% in last 3m, lots of eviction churn
Maureen: rolling up to PagerDuty, customer-visible errors? any 5xx?
Ken (SRE): 503s are low but tail-latency causes timeouts in a few upstream clients, quick check: kvcache mem usage doubled -> eviction storms
Aj: reproducing on staging with load-generator: when concurrency > 1200 we see continuous-batch coordinator thrash, microbatch jitter increases, latency cliff
Maureen: tagging customers on page: @enterprise-team will follow up with impacted accounts

sarah (oncall): immediate mitigation options: reduce batch_window_ms to 10, force microbatch_max to 8, enable kv-eviction-rate-limit hotpatch?
Ken (SRE): agree. Recommend two-step: 1) throttle ingress for non-SLA tiers to bring concurrency down, 2) land hotpatch to limit prefetch concurrency and cap kv reclaim rate
Leo: deployed temporary ingress throttle to 80% of baseline for bg-tiers (command):
```
kubectl patch cm ingress-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"global_throttle":"0.8"}}'
```
Aj: throttle applied, success: overall qps down ~22%

Maureen: Sarah, can you coordinate hotpatch landing? I can own rollout and rollback hooks
sarah (oncall): preparing patch now, going to reduce batch_window_ms from 50 -> 8 and set microbatch_max: 12 -> 6 (to reduce packing jitter)
sarah (oncall): also toggling kv_prefetch.disabled = true for prod-dedicated-1 to stop aggressive prefetch loops

Ken (SRE): patch ready, sending canary to 3 hosts in west-2 (host ids: 42,43,44). Canary route pinned to canary-hosts.
Aj: starting canary traffic reroute (~3% traffic)
Leo: canary metrics: p95 down from 2.3s -> 720ms on canary hosts, kvcache hit recovers to 82%
Maureen: roll to 25% if stable for 2 minutes
sarah (oncall): rolling to 25% now

oncall-bot: ALERT: config-change deployed to 25% canary (batch_window_ms=8, microbatch_max=6, kv_prefetch=false)

Ken (SRE): monitoring evictions: eviction-rate halved, cache size stabilizing
Aj: at 25% latency improved but overall p95 still 1.1s — because other pools still see thrash
Maureen: let's run fallback: enable model-variant-fallback to smaller KV-friendly quantized model for low-priority calls to reduce cache pressure (hotpatch)
Leo: enabling fallback rule: route match tier=bg -> model=redwood-q4f-small
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/rollouts -d '{"rule":"tier==bg","model":"redwood-q4f-small"}'
```

sarah (oncall): fallback live, observing immediate qps shift to small model for bg-tier
Ken (SRE): good, p95 across prod drops to 650ms, overall KV hit ~88% now
Maureen: customer impact check: only degraded infrequent timeouts for 5 customers; opened follow-up tickets and sent initial incident email

Aj: proposed follow-up: revert aggressive prefetch heuristics, add a short-lived eviction backoff, and add a circuit breaker at controller when queue depth > 1M ops/min
Leo: filing a telemetry ticket to capture microbatch-size distribution and per-host prefetch concurrency for later RCA
sarah (oncall): agreed. I'll keep throttle in place for 30m, then gradually lift while we monitor for regression. Rolling the canary to 100% in 10m if stable

oncall-bot: NOTE: oncall rotation handoff scheduled in 15m. @Ken (SRE) please be ready for handoff if I need to escalate

Ken (SRE): I'll take over if the throttle needs ramping or we see another eviction pulse
Maureen: sending postmortem invite, capturing key mitigations: ingress throttle, batch_window reduce, microbatch cap, kv_prefetch disable, model fallback
Aj: leaving a small script for relief oncall to quickly toggle kv_prefetch and throttle:
```
# quick-relief.sh
kubectl patch cm ingress-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"global_throttle":"1.0"}}'
kubectl set env deploy/inference-runtime -n prod KV_PREFETCH=false
```

sarah (oncall): logging timeline and actions to incident ticket INC-2026-1719. Will follow up with RCA owners. Thanks team :heart:
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by Ken (SRE)
Ken (SRE): taking post-incident ownership, will coordinate RCA and long-term fixes (eviction backoff, controller circuit, telemetry)
Maureen: agreed, also recommend a small game-day to test high-concurrency batching behavior in staging next week

oncall-bot: INCIDENT resolved: p95 back to baseline, monitoring for 60m. Auto-close suspended.
